panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Total number of Gemini CLI sessions observed in the selected time range. Helps understand overall usage volume.

panels.title: Avg API Latency
panels.description: Average API call duration in seconds over the selected time range. Alert thresholds: yellow ≥5s, red ≥15s. High values indicate latency regressions.

panels.title: Thought Tokens
panels.description: Total thought tokens consumed across all Gemini CLI sessions for the selected model(s). Thought tokens represent internal reasoning chains and directly affect cost.

panels.title: Tool Calls
panels.description: Total number of tool calls executed by Gemini CLI in the selected time range. High counts indicate active code-editing or file-manipulation sessions.

panels.title: Lines Changed
panels.description: Total lines of code changed by Gemini CLI tool calls in the selected time range. Tracks productivity impact of AI-assisted edits.

panels.title: API Requests
panels.description: Total number of API requests made to the Gemini backend in the selected time range. Useful for capacity planning and cost estimation.

panels.title: Thought Ratio
panels.description: Ratio of thought tokens to total tokens consumed. Alert thresholds: green <50%, yellow 50–80%, red >80%. A high ratio may indicate excessive internal reasoning loops.

panels.title: Input Tokens
panels.description: Total input tokens sent to the Gemini API in the selected time range for the selected model(s). Input tokens include prompts and context and drive API cost.

panels.title: Output Tokens
panels.description: Total output tokens received from the Gemini API in the selected time range for the selected model(s). Output tokens represent generated content and contribute to API cost.

panels.title: Cache Tokens
panels.description: Total cache tokens used in the selected time range. Cache hits reduce API cost by reusing previously computed context.

panels.title: Tool Tokens
panels.description: Total tokens attributed to tool-call results injected back into the prompt context. High values suggest heavy tool-augmented workflows.

panels.title: Cache Efficiency
panels.description: Ratio of cache tokens to total tokens consumed. Alert thresholds: red <50%, yellow 50–80%, green >80%. A high cache efficiency ratio reduces API cost.

panels.title: Latency by Model (P50)
panels.description: Median (P50) API call duration broken down by model in the selected time range. Alert thresholds: yellow ≥5s, red ≥15s. Use this to compare latency across models.

panels.title: Tokens by Model
panels.description: Distribution of total token consumption by model over the selected time range. Helps identify which model drives the most token usage and cost.

panels.title: Tokens by Type
panels.description: Distribution of total token consumption by token type (input, output, thought, cache, tool) over the selected time range. Useful for understanding cost composition.

panels.title: Top 10 Tools
panels.description: Top 10 tool functions called by Gemini CLI in the selected time range, ranked by call count. Reveals which capabilities are most frequently exercised.

panels.title: Tool Success / Error
panels.description: Ratio of successful to failed tool calls in the selected time range. A growing error slice indicates tool reliability issues requiring investigation.

panels.title: Top 10 Commands
panels.description: Top 10 slash commands used in Gemini CLI sessions, extracted from log events. Identifies the most frequently used user-facing commands.

panels.title: API Success / Error
panels.description: Ratio of successful (HTTP 200) to failed API requests in the selected time range. A growing error slice indicates API reliability issues.

panels.title: Routing Decisions
panels.description: Real-time log stream of model routing decisions made by Gemini CLI. Useful for debugging which model is selected for incoming requests.

panels.title: Avg Routing Latency
panels.description: Average model-routing decision latency in milliseconds. Alert thresholds: yellow ≥500ms, red ≥2000ms. High values indicate routing overhead impacting responsiveness.

panels.title: Model Breakdown
panels.description: Per-model breakdown table showing API request count, average latency, input tokens, output tokens, thought tokens, and cache tokens for the selected time range.

panels.title: Token Usage Over Time
panels.description: Token usage over time broken down by token type (input, output, thought, cache, tool). Useful for spotting sudden spikes in token consumption and understanding usage trends.

panels.title: Token Usage by Model Over Time
panels.description: Token usage over time broken down by model. Helps track which model is consuming the most tokens and how usage shifts after model changes.

panels.title: API Latency Over Time (P95)
panels.description: P95 API call duration over time. Shows the tail latency experienced by the slowest 5% of requests. Sustained high values warrant investigation.

panels.title: Tool Latency Over Time
panels.description: Average tool execution latency over time. High or increasing values indicate tool performance degradation that may slow down AI-assisted workflows.

panels.title: Operation Duration (P50/P95/P99)
panels.description: API operation duration percentiles (P50, P95, P99) over time. Comparing percentiles reveals the shape of the latency distribution and helps identify outlier spikes.

panels.title: Tool Latency Heatmap
panels.description: Heatmap of tool execution latency distribution over time. Darker cells indicate more frequent occurrences at that latency bucket, revealing latency hotspots.

panels.title: Tool Execution Details
panels.description: Live log stream of individual tool execution events from Gemini CLI. Useful for debugging tool failures or inspecting tool call arguments and results.

panels.title: API Call Details
panels.description: Live log stream of API call events from Gemini CLI. Useful for debugging API errors, inspecting request headers, and tracing individual requests.

panels.title: Event Stream
panels.description: Full event stream from the Gemini CLI service. Use this for broad exploration of all log events when debugging unexpected behaviour.
